ex-407-1.title: A magnet passing through a coil
ex-407-1.question: A bar magnet passes through a coil as shown. Draw the direction of the induced current I through the coil when the magnet is (a) approaching the coil, (b) at the centre of the coil, (c) leaving the coil. Hence, determine which end of the resistor, X or Y, is at a higher potential.
ex-407-1.answer:
(a)

End X is at a higher potential.

(b)

There is no induced current. X and Y are at the same potential.

(c)

End Y is at a higher potential.
ex-407-1.tips:
Tip

Current flows from a position of higher potential to a position of lower potential in the external circuit.

ex-407-2.title: A coil entering a uniform magnetic field
ex-407-2.question:
A retangular metal coil PQRS is entering a uniform magnetic field which points into the page.

(a) Explain the direction of the induced current in the coil.

(b) Explain whether a current is induced when the coil is completely inside the field.
ex-407-2.answer:
(a) As the coil moves, it encloses more and more magnetic field lines that point into the page.

According to Lenz’s law, to oppose this change, the induced current flows in a direction to produce field lines that point out of the page.

By the right-hand grip rule, the induced current flows anticlockwise.

(b) No current is induced in the coil. This is because the number of field lines enclosed by the coil remains unchanged.

ex-407-4.title:  HKDSE 2014 Paper 1A Q27 A coil beside a straight wire
ex-407-4.question:
A coil PQRS is placed next to a long straight wire XY as shown.

Which of the following can generate a clockwise induced current in PQRS?

(1) A steady current flows from Y to X.

(2) A current flows from X to Y and is decreasing in magnitude.

(3) A current flows from Y to X and is increasing in magnitude.

A (1) only B (2) only

C (2) and (3) only D (1), (2) and (3)
ex-407-4.answer:
When the current is steady, the magnetic field through PQRS does not change, so no current is induced.

∴ (1) is incorrect.

When a current flows from X to Y, by the right-hand grip rule, the magnetic field points into the page through PQRS. When the current decreases, the magnetic field decreases. By Lenz’s law, the induced current produces a magnetic field pointing into the page to oppose the change. By the right-hand grip rule again, the induced current flows clockwise.

∴ (2) is correct.

Similarly, when a current flows from Y to X, the magnetic field points out of the page through PQRS. When the current increases, the induced current produces a magnetic field pointing into the page to oppose the change.

∴ (3) is correct.

∴ The answer is C.

ex-407-5.title: A bar magnet falling through a coil
ex-407-5.question:
A bar magnet with its N-pole pointing downwards is dropped and passes through a coil (Fig a). A voltage sensor is used to record the induced e.m.f. ε in the coil. Figure b shows how ε varies with time.

(a) Explain why ε changes sign in the process.

(b) Explain why the negative peak is larger in magnitude than the positive peak.

(c) State what happens to the graph if

(i) the polarity of the magnet is reversed;

(ii) the coil is replaced by another coil with more turns.

(d) If the coil is connected to a 1-Ω resistor instead of the voltage sensor, will the magnet fall faster or slower?
ex-407-5.answer:
(a) By Lenz’s law, when the magnet is approaching the upper end of the coil, the e.m.f. induced tends to make the upper end an N-pole to oppose the approaching N-pole of the magnet. When the magnet is leaving the lower end of the coil, the induced e.m.f. tends to make the lower end an N-pole to attract the leaving S-pole of the magnet. Hence ε changes sign.

(b) The magnet speeds up as it falls under gravity and therefore leaves the coil at a higher speed. This causes a higher rate of change in the magnetic flux through the coil and produces a larger magnitude of ε.

(c) (i) The graph becomes upside down.

(ii) Both the positive and negative peaks become larger in magnitude.

(d) Since the resistance of the circuit will decrease, the induced current will increase. The magnet will be opposed by larger magnetic forces and will fall slower.

ex-407-7.title: Calculation of flux linkage
ex-407-7.question:
A 10-turn coil of area 4 cm2 is placed in a uniform magnetic field of flux density 2 × 10–3 T. Find the flux linkage through the coil if

(a) the normal of the coil is parallel to the field (Fig a);

(b) the normal of the coil makes an angle of 30° to the field (Fig b).
ex-407-7.answer:
(a) Flux linkage = NΦ = N(BA) = (10)(2 × 10–3)(4 × 10–4) = 8 × 10–6 Wb

(b) Flux linkage = NBA cos θ = (8 × 10–6) cos 30° = 6.93 × 10–6 Wb

ex-407-8.title: A changing magnetic field and a rotating coil  HKDSE 2019 Paper 1B Q9(b)
ex-407-8.question:
A 10-turn square coil of area 0.01 m2 is inside a uniform magnetic field of 4 mT pointing into the page (Fig a). Find the average value of the induced e.m.f. in the coil if

(a) the magnetic field decreases to zero in 0.2 s;

(b) the magnetic field decreases to zero, reverses in direction and becomes 4 mT out of the page in 0.2 s (Fig b);

(c) the coil is rotated by 180° in 0.5 s (Fig c).
ex-407-8.answer:
(a) ε = Δ(NΦ)Δt = Δ(NBA)Δt = NA × ΔBΔt = (10)(0.01)(4 × 10–3 − 00.2) = 2 × 10–3 V

(b) ΔΦ = Δ(BA) = (4 × 10–3)(0.01) – [–(4 × 10–3)(0.01)] = 8 × 10–5 Wb

ε = N ΔΦΔt = (10)(8 × 10–50.2) = 4 × 10–3 V

(c) ΔΦ = 8 × 10–5 Wb

ε = N ΔΦΔt = (10)(8 × 10–50.5) = 1.6 × 10–3 V
ex-407-8.tips:
Tip

Use the magnitude of ΔB in calculating the magnitude of ε.

Tip

When B reverses in direction, it passes through the coil in the opposite direction, so Φ changes from BA to –BA.

Tip

After the coil is rotated by 180°, B passes through it in the opposite direction, so ΔΦ is the same as that in (b).
ex-407-8.think: What is the average value of ε when the coil in (c) is rotated by 90° in 0.25 s?
ex-407-8.thinkAnswer: The flux per turn changes from BA to zero. The magnitude of the average induced e.m.f. is ε¯=N|ΔΦ|Δ t=10(4×10−3)(0.01)0.25=1.6×10−3 V.

ex-407-9.title: Rate of flux cutting
ex-407-9.question: A conducting loop PQRS moves at a constant speed of 0.04 m s–1 and enters a uniform magnetic field of 2 mT. Find the magnitude of the induced e.m.f. across QR when the coil is entering the field.
ex-407-9.answer:
In time Δt, the change in area of the loop inside the field is

ΔA = 0.1 × vΔt = 0.1(0.04)Δt = 0.004Δt

ε = ΔΦΔt = Δ(BA)Δt = B × ΔAΔt = (2 × 10–3) × 0.004ΔtΔt = 8 × 10–6 V
ex-407-9.think:
1 What is the direction of the induced current?

2 What is ε when the loop is completely inside the field?
ex-407-9.thinkAnswer:
1 Anticlockwise, R → Q → P → S → R. As the loop enters the field, the magnetic flux into the page increases. By Lenz’s law, the induced current produces a field out of the page to oppose that increase.

2 The net induced e.m.f. around the complete loop is zero: its area in the uniform field and hence its flux are constant. There is no induced current. A distinction is needed because the original question mentions QR: the motional e.m.f. of the moving side QR itself remains BLv=8×10−6 V, but the equal contribution from PS opposes it around the circuit.
